en.title: Word Pairs That Are Equal or Prefixes of Each Other
en.description:
Count unordered pairs of distinct indices i<j such that the two words are equal, or one is a prefix of the other. Identical words at different indices are still counted separately.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n words. The source gives no character or length bounds; on this site 1≤n≤100000, and words contain only lowercase English letters with length 1..30.
en.explanation: Example 1: back pairs with backdoor and backgammon, 2 pairs, and come pairs with comeback, 1 pair, for 3 in total. Example 2: the two a's form 1 pair with each other, and each forms pairs with abc, ab and ac, giving 6 pairs; ab and abc form 1 more, for 8 in total. Example 3: three distinct indices pair up with each other, for 3 in total.
hints: Sort lexicographically. Taking each word as the earlier one, all words starting with it form a contiguous range; binary search the insertion position of word plus the character { as the right end of the range, and count only words after the current position.
